title: KV-Prefix Log Adapter: order-preserving fanout with schema negotiation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight KV-prefix adapter that accepts polyglot log payloads, extracts a stable ordering key (sequence or monotonic marker), normalizes fields for downstream Loki and ELK consumers, and fans out to tenant-specific topics without breaking event order. This component sits between edge log producers and the central log fabric and solves two problems: 1) lossless ordered delivery to long-tail sinks, and 2) schema negotiation/field enrichment for structured and semi-structured logs.
background: We continue to see production issues where processing re-ordering and schema drift cause noisy dashboards and missed trace joins. Current ad-hoc shims either rewrite IDs (breaking deterministic replays) or drop unknown fields (breaking observability for new services). We need a small, high-throughput adapter that preserves producer ordering while allowing downstream consumers to evolve independently.
goals: 1) Preserve per-producer order for all records routed to the same tenant/sink. 2) Emit a normalized minimal schema for Loki labels and an exploded JSON document for ELK. 3) Provide a negotiation mode where unknown fields are forwarded to a tombstone store for schema inspection. 4) Backpressure safely to producers under downstream pressure while minimizing message duplication.
non_goals: Full schema registry or heavy-weight transformation engine. This adapter should not perform ML-based enrichment or field-level redaction beyond configurable allowlists/deny-lists.
proposed_solution: Introduce a stateless adapter that: (a) computes a KV-prefix routing key composed of tenant_id + producer_id + sequence_slot (sequence_slot derived from monotonic counters or event timestamp buckets), (b) advertises schema fingerprints to a lightweight registry service, (c) tags messages with canonical trace_link (if available) and preserves original producer_id and sequence metadata in headers, (d) fans out to Kafka topics partitioned by tenant+slot to maintain ordering, and (e) exposes a fast path for 'pass-through' mode when messages already conform to the canonical schema.
architecture_decisions:
- Ordering guarantee will be per-producer-per-tenant; cross-producer order is not preserved.
- Use Kafka partition key of tenant_id||producer_id so single-producer partitions are contiguous.
- For producers without sequence counters, fall back to timestamp-bucketed slots and mark as 'approx_order'.
- Maintain a tombstone topic for unknown fields with a sample payload for offline schema extraction.
- Adapter will not persist long-term state; rely on Kafka partitions and consumer-side compacted indices for replays.
implementation_steps: Prototype adapter binary (Golang) with pluggable parsers: JSON, newline-delimited keyvals, protobuf-raw.
Add sequence-slot calculation module and header propagation for original-producer-seq and orig-ts.
Implement schema fingerprint emitter to tombstone topic and small HTTP API to fetch recent fingerprints.
Enable configurable allowlist/denylist for fields to avoid PII leakage; integrate with KMS for masking rules reference.
Wire adapter into existing ingress fleet behind edge LB and validate end-to-end to Kafka topic topology.
Add consumer adapters for Loki label mapping and an ELK-transform lambda that expands canonical fields into _source.
Create migration scripts and rollback plan for producers that switch to adapter pass-through mode.
acceptance_criteria: Ability to replay a producer's 1M events with preserved order and no duplicate sequence numbers in downstream store.
Loki dashboards for the canary tenant show identical trace link joins pre/post adapter within 5% error margin.
Tombstone topic contains sampled unknown-field payloads and a visible fingerprint table in Confluence.
Backpressure behavior: when downstream Kafka is congested, adapter responds with 429 to producers using HTTP with Retry-After and metrics emit queue_depth > 0 but no silent drops.
Security review completed and allowlist policy validated for top 20 customers.
Automated integration test covering JSON/protobuf/newline formats and sequence-less fallback path.
Latency SLA: median adapter processing < 5ms, p99 < 50ms under normal load (1000 events/s per instance).
canary_and_rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal telemetry team only (single tenant) for 48h. Stage 2: two low-traffic customers (48-72h). Stage 3: 10% traffic ramp targeting tenant-partitioned Kafka. Each stage uses canary metrics: ordering-violation-rate, tombstone-rate, adapter-latency. Automatic rollback trigger if ordering-violation-rate > 0.01% or tombstone-rate growth indicates schema explosion.
testing_plan: Unit tests for parsers and slot calculation, load test harness using k6 to simulate bursty producers, end-to-end replay test using a dedicated Kafka cluster, and a chaos test that kills adapter instances to verify producer retry behavior.
security_and_compliance_notes: Must redact fields matching denylist patterns before forwarding to non-EU clusters. KMS integration required for masking keys; security review ticket linked in comments. Ensure tombstone topic is compacted and access-controlled.
open_risks: Producers that don't include any monotonic counter will have only approximate ordering which may confuse consumers expecting strict ordering.
Tombstone topic could grow quickly if many producers emit ad-hoc fields; need sampling and TTL.
Latency spikes when schema fingerprint service is slow; consider local LRU cache with TTL.
Coordination required with platform teams to re-partition Kafka or create tenant-topics for large customers.
